intro: North Korea shares thousands of years of Korean history with the South, but since 1948 it has been one of the world's most closed and tightly controlled states.

chapters.title: One Korea
text: Korean kingdoms such as Goguryeo, which ruled much of the north and Manchuria, Goryeo and Joseon shaped a shared language and culture. Pyongyang was Goguryeo's capital.
Japan ruled Korea harshly from 1910 to 1945.

chapters.title: Division and war
text: After Japan's defeat in 1945, the Soviet Union occupied the north and the US the south. In 1948 two states were declared, and Kim Il Sung led the North.

In 1950 North Korea invaded the South, starting the Korean War. China fought on the North's side and a US-led UN force on the South's. Millions died, and an armistice in 1953 stopped the fighting but no peace treaty was signed.

highlight.title: Still at war
highlight.text: Technically, the Korean War has never formally ended.

chapters.title: The Kim dynasty
text: Kim Il Sung was followed by his son Kim Jong Il in 1994 and grandson Kim Jong Un in 2011. A famine in the 1990s killed hundreds of thousands, possibly more.
North Korea has tested nuclear weapons since 2006, leading to UN sanctions. In 2024 it sent troops to help Russia in its war against Ukraine.

timeline.title: Goguryeo
timeline.text: A northern Korean kingdom is founded, by tradition.

keyTerms.meaning: An agreement to stop fighting, not a peace treaty.
Democratic People's Republic of Korea, the official name.
